props.title: Cry-Baby

sections.content: John Waters' Cry-Baby brilliantly subverts 1950s teen musicals through his signature trash-culture lens. Johnny Depp stars as Wade "Cry-Baby" Walker, a leather-clad greaser who can shed a single perfect tear, leading his gang of "drapes" against the square "squares." Waters deliberately flips Grease (1978) on its head - instead of the bad boy conforming to society, Cry-Baby proudly maintains his rebel status while good girl Allison (Amy Locane) embraces her wild side. The film wickedly parodies Elvis movies like Jailhouse Rock (1957) while celebrating genuine rockabilly culture.

sections.content: Waters assembled an incredible cast of counterculture icons for Cry-Baby, including punk pioneer Iggy Pop, former porn star Traci Lords, and cult actress Susan Tyrrell. The musical numbers gleefully mock West Side Story (1961) and Bye Bye Birdie (1963) while delivering legitimate rockabilly bangers. Waters' Baltimore becomes a heightened playground where juvenile delinquents are the heroes and respectability is the real crime. The film's influence can be seen in later teen musical satires like But I'm a Cheerleader (1999) and Crybaby (2020).

The film's costume and production design by Van Smith perfectly captures both the squeaky-clean and greaser aesthetics of the 1950s while subtly exaggerating them for comic effect. This attention to period detail mixed with camp sensibility influenced later works like Pleasantville (1998) and Down with Love (2003). Waters proves you can simultaneously mock and celebrate a genre, creating something both satirical and genuinely entertaining. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Teen Musical Satire

sections.content: Cry-Baby helped pave the way for more subversive teen musicals like Hedwig and the Angry Inch (2001) and Repo! The Genetic Opera (2008). Waters' ability to blend social commentary with outrageous musical numbers influenced everything from Chicago (2002) to Moulin Rouge! (2001). The film's celebration of outsiders and rejection of conformity resonates with later works like Scott Pilgrim vs. the World (2010).
